result:
The final cache scores 0.558 on the search split, up from the 0.365 baseline, using 10 of the 24 scorer calls. It is saved as `final.py`.

I used about 4 minutes of the roughly 15 I had planned, and stopped because several variants had plateaued at 0.557–0.558. I did not run a held-out check, since I was only given the search split.

`final.py` runs six cache policies as shadow simulations on every request and follows whichever has had the most hits recently. The real cache converges to the leader's contents. Following a policy that holds a mix of recent keys and heavily used keys means the real cache can hit on keys the leader has already dropped.

The six policies are an ARC (adaptive recency/frequency) cache, an LFU-style admission cache with several window sizes, and one tuned for rarer admissions. The LFU-style admission policies keep a stable part of a loop larger than the cache, while ARC does best on recency-heavy traces.

| Candidate | Search score |
|---|---|
| LRU baseline (given) | 0.365 |
| ARC | 0.407 |
| Window plus frequency-based admission | 0.510 |
| Same, with an adaptive window | 0.452 (the adaptation hurt shifting loops) |
| Mix of 2 policies (first champion) | 0.544 |
| Mix of 4 policies | 0.552 |
| Mix of 6 policies (final) | 0.558 |

Two further variants changed little. Retuning how fast the mix switches gave 0.557 both ways, and adding a seventh policy that inserts new keys at the eviction end gave 0.557.

Per-trace hit rates for the final pick:

| Trace | Hit rate |
|---|---|
| hot_with_scans | 0.246 |
| loop_and_hot | 0.636 |
| phases | 0.641 |
| mixed | 0.280 |
| recency | 0.846 |
| shifting_loops | 0.702 |

hot_with_scans and mixed barely moved across every variant, so they may be near their ceiling; I couldn't tell without knowing the traces.

My local harness used synthetic traces I made up from the task description. Its absolute numbers didn't match the scorer's, so I leaned on the scorer calls and used the harness only for sanity and speed checks. CPU time for the final file on 12 traces of 30,000 requests was about 1.2s, well under the 8s limit.
